english.title: Possess a launcher - military equipment
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the authority of the Secretary of State, had in your possession a launcher, namely **(..SPECIFY APPARATUS..), not falling within section 5(1)(ae) of the Firearms Act 1968, and which was designed to be used with a rocket or ammunition for military use which consisted in or incorporated a missile designed to explode on or immediately before impact or ammunition containing or designed or adapted to contain any noxious liquid, gas or other thing
english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1A)(c) of, and Schedule 6 to, the Firearms Act 1968.

english.notes:
(i) Section 5(7)(a) of the Firearms Act 1968 provides that a rocket or ammunition is to be taken for military use if it is designed to be capable of being used with a military weapon.
(ii) Section 5A contains exemptions.
(iii) See also offence wordings: H2783, H2784, H2785, H2786 and H2787.
(iv) On conviction for this offence, the court can order the forfeiture or disposal of any firearm or ammunition and cancellation of any firearm certificate or shot gun certificate, and any firearm or ammunition subject of such order may be seized or detained by a constable (section 52 of the Firearms Act 1968).

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 282(2) and (3) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

For offences committed on or after 12th March 2015 the fine on summary conviction is unlimited, see section 85 of the Legal Aid, Sentencing and Punishment of Offenders Act 2012.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
